Découverte en 1801 et d'abord classée pa: Discovered in 1801 and first counted among the planets, Ceres has been a dwarf planet since 2006. About 950 km across, it is the largest object in the asteroid belt, between Mars and Jupiter: on its own it holds roughly a quarter to a third of the belt's mass. The Dawn probe entered orbit around it on 6 March 2015, the first spacecraft to orbit a dwarf planet.
En 1990, les ingénieurs Robert Zubrin et: In 1990, engineers Robert Zubrin and David Baker proposed “Mars Direct”: first send a return vehicle with empty tanks. On site, it makes its own fuel, methane and oxygen, from Martian air and a little hydrogen brought from Earth: about 18 kg for 1 kg of hydrogen. The crew only leaves once the tanks are full.
En 2008, l'atterrisseur Phoenix a mesuré: In 2008, the Phoenix lander measured about 0.4 to 0.6 % perchlorates in the Martian soil. These salts are toxic to humans and hinder crops: regolith must be washed before use.
En 2017, des ingénieurs de l'ESA ont imp: In 2017, ESA engineers 3D-printed a 20 × 10 × 3 cm brick from simulated lunar soil: 147 mirrors focused sunlight to heat each thin layer to around 1,000 °C. It took about five hours. The brick is roughly as strong as plaster.
En 2017, le spectromètre de Dawn a repér: In 2017, Dawn's spectrometer spotted the signature of aliphatic organic matter (carbon chains) near Ernutet crater, over about 1,000 km². It was the first clear detection of organic molecules from orbit on a main-belt body. Their exact nature is still unknown; they may come from inside Ceres.
En 2017, à l'université de Wageningen, W: In 2017, at Wageningen University, Wieger Wamelink put adult earthworms in a Martian soil simulant supplied by NASA, enriched with pig slurry and planted with rocket. At the end of the experiment, a surprise: two young worms! With the manure, the simulant even did better than the control sand. Worms also help water soak into the soil.
En 2018, au Nevada, la NASA a testé KRUS: In 2018, in Nevada, NASA tested KRUSTY, a small fission reactor whose core, at around 800 °C, drove Stirling engines: about 1 kilowatt of electricity. The final test ran for 28 hours at full power. The Kilopower project aims for up to 10 kW for at least 10 years; according to NASA, four units would be enough for an outpost.
En 2019, la NASA publie une « carte au t: In 2019, NASA published a “treasure map” of Martian ice, built from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and Mars Odyssey probes: in places, water ice may lie just 2.5 cm below the surface. The Arcadia Planitia plain, in the north, stands out as a promising site for astronauts. A shovel would do, says researcher Sylvain Piqueux.
En 2023, la NASA a annoncé que le systèm: In 2023, NASA announced that the Space Station's life-support system recovers about 98 % of its water, including from the astronauts' urine and sweat.
En janvier 2005, le rover Opportunity id: In January 2005, the Opportunity rover identified “Heat Shield Rock”, a basketball-sized rock made mostly of iron and nickel: the first meteorite identified on another planet. It lay near the debris of the rover's own heat shield.
En juin 2008, l'atterrisseur Phoenix a c: In June 2008, the Phoenix lander dug a trench and uncovered white chunks. Within four days they were gone: they had sublimated, turning straight from ice into vapour. Proof that they were water ice.
En juin 2018, une tempête de poussière a: In June 2018, a dust storm covered the whole planet. The solar-powered Opportunity rover, designed for 90 days, had driven more than 45 km in 15 years: deprived of light, it fell silent. The nuclear-powered Curiosity rover was not affected.

L'air que nous respirons contient 78 % d: The air we breathe is 78% nitrogen: this inert gas fills the atmosphere around the oxygen. Martian air is 95% CO₂; nitrogen makes up only about 2.6% of it (measured by the Curiosity rover's SAM instrument), and surface pressure there is less than 1% of Earth's. Titan, on the other hand, is wrapped in nitrogen: about 95% of its atmosphere, at a pressure 60% higher than Earth's. On Ceres, the Dawn probe spotted clays and salts containing ammonia, a nitrogen molecule.

L'instrument MOXIE, à bord du rover Pers: The MOXIE instrument, aboard the Perseverance rover, split Martian CO₂ into oxygen and carbon monoxide. From 2021 to 2023 it produced 122 g of oxygen in 16 runs, up to 12 g per hour, at 98 % purity or better.
L'électrolyse sépare l'eau : 2 H₂O → 2 H: Electrolysis splits water: 2 H₂O → 2 H₂ + O₂. Since oxygen is much heavier than hydrogen, 9 kg of water give 8 kg of oxygen. This is how the International Space Station makes most of its air.

Le 14 janvier 2005, la sonde européenne: On 14 January 2005, the European Huygens probe landed on Titan, Saturn's largest moon: the first landing in the outer Solar System. It measured a pressure about 1.5 times that of Earth's air and a temperature of −179 °C. The atmosphere is about 95 % nitrogen and 5 % methane.
Le 1er septembre 2021, Perseverance prél: On 1 September 2021, Perseverance took its first core of Martian rock, barely thicker than a pencil, from a rock nicknamed “Rochette”. A first attempt in August had failed: the rock crumbled into powder. Sealed in a titanium tube, the sample awaits a future mission to bring it back to Earth.
Le 24 décembre 2021, le sismomètre de l': On 24 December 2021, the InSight lander's seismometer recorded a magnitude 4 marsquake. The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter then found the cause: a meteorite had dug a crater about 150 m wide in Amazonis Planitia, next to Arcadia, throwing out blocks of water ice. Ice had never been seen so close to the equator.
Le cœur d'un petit réacteur comme KRUSTY: The core of a small reactor like KRUSTY runs at around 800 °C: its heat, instead of being lost in the radiators, helps bake the regolith.
Le dôme est vide tant qu'il manque d'azo: The dome stays empty while it lacks nitrogen. A Martian compressor gets very little: have some shipped from Titan or Ceres.

Le four à régolithe transforme la poussi: The regolith kiln turns Martian dust into building materials, in exchange for a lot of energy.

Le gaz neutre qui remplit l'air des gran: The inert gas that fills the air of large domes, around the oxygen. Martian air holds almost none: Titan is made of it, and Ceres's salts contain some.

Pour aller d'une planète à l'autre avec: To travel between planets with the least fuel, spacecraft follow a Hohmann transfer orbit: half an ellipse around the Sun. The planets must also be well placed: between Earth and Mars, these “launch windows” come round about every 26 months, and the journey takes 7 to 9 months. Perseverance took about six and a half months.

Pourrait-on réchauffer Mars en libérant: Could Mars be warmed by releasing the CO₂ in its polar caps and soil? In 2018, Bruce Jakosky and Christopher Edwards did the maths using data from several probes: even by processing every source on the planet, the pressure would only reach about 7 % of Earth's. With today's technology, terraforming Mars is out of reach.

Titan a des mers à sa surface, mais de m: Titan has seas on its surface, but of liquid methane and ethane. In 2014, the Cassini probe's radar sounded Ligeia Mare: about 160 m deep at its centre, and a liquid so pure that the waves passed straight through it. Kraken Mare, the largest sea, holds about 80 % of the surface liquids on its own; at its centre it was too deep for the radar.
